newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine tycoons drop airport terminal project.
newsitem.headline: Philippine tycoons drop airport terminal project.

text.p: Asia's Emerging Dragon Corp (AEDC), a company owned by the country's six richest Chinese-Filipino tycoons said on Tuesday it had dropped a plan to bid for the construction of a new passenger terminal at Manila airport.
The company was invited by President Fidel Ramos in 1992 to build a modern terminal at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport in Manila under a build-operate-transfer scheme.
The firm had accepted the offer, but a new group led by a local firm People's Aircargo & Warehousing Co Inc (Paircargo) submitted a better bid earlier this year.
Other members of the People's Aircargo consortium are Philippine Airport and Ground Services Inc and Security Bank Corp.
The transportation department had asked AEDC to match the offer of People's Aircargo. It had given AEDC until Tuesday to match the offer.

"(AEDC) has decided not to respond to the Department of Transportation and Communications' (DOTC) call for it to match the proposal of the People's Aircargo consortium," the company said in a statement.
It said the department and the bidding committee did not provide enough information on the bid for it to match the offer.

"This unfortunate situation deters and frustrates AEDC from making an intelligent assessment of what it has been requested to match," Arthur Villaraza, the company's counsel, said in a letter to transportation secretary Amado Lagdameo.

The AEDC also questioned the capability of the consortium to raise the 2.7 billion peso equity for the project. It also questioned the possibility of hiring a foreign firm to be the terminal operator.

"This is a violation not only of the bidding rules, but also fo the provision of the Philippine Constitution. Foreign participation in comapnies operating a public utility is limited to 40 percent under our law," the company said.

"Despite this development, AEDC will monitor closely further actions by DOTC on the matter, particularly the terms of the concesison agreements that the DOTC may enter into, to assure full compliance to the rules," it added.

Partners in AEDC are beer and cigarette taipan Lucio Tan, mall magnate Henry Sy of SM Prime Holdings, bankers George Ty of Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co Inc and Alfonso Yuchengco of House of Investments, real estate kingpin Andrew Gotianun of Filinvest Development Corp and consumer food manufacturer John Gokongwei of JG Summit Holdings.
